chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, who said:

Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) was asked about the speckled crow, so he said: 'It is not eaten.' He said: 'And who permitted the black one for you?' And this report does not contradict what was narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating speckled versus black crows according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes the impermissibility of the speckled crow (*al-ghurab al-abqa*) while critically examining the permissibility of the black crow, highlighting the Shia scholarly method of distinguishing between similar species based on specific textual evidence rather than generalization. This ruling underscores the precision in *fiqh al-hayawan* (jurisprudence of animals), where the presence of distinct physical markers can determine edibility, a principle consistent with other hadiths that do not contradict this specific distinction.
